30: pub fn load_workspace(
31:     general_options: &GeneralOptions,
32:     project_options: &ProjectOptions,
33:     load_options: &LoadOptions,
34: ) -> anyhow::Result<(hir::Crate, ide::AnalysisHost, vfs::Vfs, ide::Edition)> {
35:     let project_path = project_options.manifest_path.as_path().canonicalize()?;
36: 
37:     // See: https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/13909
38:     // The `canonicalize` func on windows will return `r"\\?\"` verbatim prefix.
39:     // "The Cargo makes a core assumption that verbatim paths aren't used."
40:     // So we need to `simplify` the path as the non-verbatim path.
41:     let project_path = dunce::simplified(&project_path).to_path_buf();
42: 
43:     let cargo_config = cargo_config(project_options, load_options);
44:     let load_config = load_config();
45: 
46:     let progress = |string| {
47:         tracing::trace!("Progress: {}", string);
48:     };
49: 
50:     let mut project_workspace = load_project_workspace(&project_path, &cargo_config, &progress)?;
51: 
52:     let (package, target) = select_package_and_target(&project_workspace, project_options)?;
53: 
54:     if general_options.verbose {
55:         eprintln!();
56:         eprintln!("crate");
57:         eprintln!("└── package: {}", package.name);
58:         eprintln!("    └── target: {}", target.name);
59:         eprintln!();
60:     }
61: 
62:     let edition = package.edition;
63: 
64:     if load_config.load_out_dirs_from_check {
65:         let build_scripts = project_workspace.run_build_scripts(&cargo_config, &progress)?;
66:         project_workspace.set_build_scripts(build_scripts)

68: 
69:     let (db, vfs, _proc_macro_client) =
70:         ra_ap_load_cargo::load_workspace(project_workspace, &cargo_config.extra_env, &load_config)?;

72:     let host = ide::AnalysisHost::with_database(db);

74:     let krate = find_crate(host.raw_database(), &vfs, &target)?;

410: pub fn find_crate(
411:     db: &ide::RootDatabase,
412:     vfs: &vfs::Vfs,
413:     target: &project_model::TargetData,
414: ) -> anyhow::Result<hir::Crate> {
415:     let crates = hir::Crate::all(db);
416: 
417:     let target_root_path = target.root.as_path();
418: 
419:     let krate = crates.into_iter().find(|krate| {
420:         let vfs_path = vfs.file_path(krate.root_file(db));
421:         let crate_root_path = vfs_path.as_path().unwrap();
422: 
423:         crate_root_path == target_root_path
424:     });
425: 
426:     krate.ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Crate not found"))
427: }

503: ) -> Option<String> {
504:     let mut path = String::new();
505: 
506:     let krate = krate(module_def_hir, db);

508:     // Obtain the crate's name (unless it's a builtin type, which have no crate):
509:     if let Some(crate_name) = krate.map(|krate| crate_name(krate, db)) {
510:         path.push_str(&crate_name);
511:     }

513:     // Obtain the item's canonicalized name:
514:     let relative_path = match module_def_hir {
515:         hir::ModuleDef::Function(function_hir) => {
516:             if let Some(assoc_item_hir) = function_hir.as_assoc_item(db) {

518:             } else {
519:                 hir::ModuleDef::Function(function_hir).canonical_path(db, edition)
520:             }
521:         }
522:         hir::ModuleDef::Const(const_hir) => {
523:             if let Some(assoc_item_hir) = const_hir.as_assoc_item(db) {
524:                 assoc_item_path(assoc_item_hir, db, edition)
525:             } else {
526:                 hir::ModuleDef::Const(const_hir).canonical_path(db, edition)
527:             }
528:         }

530:             if let Some(assoc_item_hir) = type_alias_hir.as_assoc_item(db) {
531:                 assoc_item_path(assoc_item_hir, db, edition)

533:                 hir::ModuleDef::TypeAlias(type_alias_hir).canonical_path(db, edition)
534:             }
535:         }
536:         hir::ModuleDef::BuiltinType(builtin_type_hir) => {
537:             Some(builtin_type_hir.name().display(db, edition).to_string())
538:         }
539:         module_def_hir => module_def_hir.canonical_path(db, edition),
540:     };
541: 
542:     if let Some(relative_path) = relative_path {
543:         if !path.is_empty() {
544:             path.push_str("::");
545:         }
546:         path.push_str(&relative_path);
547:     }
548: 
549:     if path.is_empty() { None } else { Some(path) }

552: fn assoc_item_path(
553:     assoc_item_hir: hir::AssocItem,
554:     db: &ide::RootDatabase,
555:     edition: ide::Edition,
556: ) -> Option<String> {
557:     let name = match assoc_item_hir {
558:         hir::AssocItem::Function(function_hir) => hir::ModuleDef::Function(function_hir)
559:             .name(db)
560:             .map(|name| name.display(db, edition).to_string()),
561:         hir::AssocItem::Const(const_hir) => hir::ModuleDef::Const(const_hir)
562:             .name(db)
563:             .map(|name| name.display(db, edition).to_string()),
564:         hir::AssocItem::TypeAlias(type_alias_hir) => hir::ModuleDef::TypeAlias(type_alias_hir)
565:             .name(db)
566:             .map(|name| name.display(db, edition).to_string()),
567:     };
568: 
569:     let name = name?;
570: 
571:     let container_path = match assoc_item_hir.container(db) {
572:         hir::AssocItemContainer::Trait(trait_hir) => {
573:             hir::ModuleDef::Trait(trait_hir).canonical_path(db, edition)
574:         }
575:         hir::AssocItemContainer::Impl(impl_hir) => impl_hir
576:             .self_ty(db)
577:             .as_adt()
578:             .and_then(|adt_hir| hir::ModuleDef::Adt(adt_hir).canonical_path(db, edition)),
579:     };
580: 
581:     let container_path = container_path?;
582: 
583:     Some(format!("{container_path}::{name}"))

586: // https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/36a70b7435c48837018c71576d7bb4e8f763f501/crates/syntax/src/ast/make.rs#L821
587: pub(crate) fn parse_ast<N: syntax::AstNode>(text: &str) -> N {
588:     let parse = syntax::SourceFile::parse(text, ide::Edition::CURRENT);
589:     let node = match parse.tree().syntax().descendants().find_map(N::cast) {
590:         Some(it) => it,
591:         None => {
592:             let node = std::any::type_name::<N>();
593:             panic!("Failed to make ast node `{node}` from text {text}")
594:         }
595:     };
596:     let node = node.clone_subtree();
597:     assert_eq!(node.syntax().text_range().start(), 0.into());
598:     node
599: }
600: 
601: pub(crate) fn parse_use_tree(path_expr: &str) -> ast::UseTree {
602:     parse_ast(&format!("use {path_expr};"))
603: }
604: 
605: pub(crate) fn parse_path_expr(path_expr: &str) -> ast::Path {
606:     parse_ast(path_expr)
607: }
608: 
609: pub(crate) fn use_tree_matches_item_path(use_tree: &ast::UseTree, item_path: &str) -> bool {
610:     if item_path.is_empty() {
611:         return false;
612:     }
613:     let node_path: ast::Path = parse_path_expr(item_path);
614:     use_tree_matches_path(use_tree, &node_path)
615: }
616: 
617: pub(crate) fn use_tree_matches_path(use_tree: &ast::UseTree, path: &ast::Path) -> bool {
618:     let mut path_segments_iter = path.segments();
619: 
620:     if let Some(use_tree_path) = use_tree.path() {
621:         for use_tree_segment in use_tree_path.segments() {
622:             match path_segments_iter.next() {
623:                 Some(path_segment) => {
624:                     if use_tree_segment.syntax().text() == path_segment.syntax().text() {
625:                         continue;
626:                     } else {
627:                         return false;
628:                     }
629:                 }
630:                 None => {
631:                     return false;
632:                 }
633:             }
634:         }
635:     }
636: 
637:     let path_segments: Vec<_> = path_segments_iter.collect();
638: 
639:     if path_segments.is_empty() {
640:         return use_tree.is_simple_path() || tree_contains_self(use_tree);
641:     }
642: 
643:     if use_tree.star_token().is_some() {
644:         return path_segments.len() == 1;
645:     }
646: 
647:     let path_suffix = ast::make::path_from_segments(path_segments, false);
648: 
649:     use_tree
650:         .use_tree_list()
651:         .into_iter()
652:         .flat_map(|list| list.use_trees())
653:         .any(|use_tree| use_tree_matches_path(&use_tree, &path_suffix))
654: }
655: 
656: fn path_is_self(path: &ast::Path) -> bool {
657:     path.segment().and_then(|seg| seg.self_token()).is_some() && path.qualifier().is_none()
658: }
659: 
660: fn tree_is_self(tree: &ast::UseTree) -> bool {
661:     tree.path().as_ref().map(path_is_self).unwrap_or(false)
662: }
663: 
664: fn tree_contains_self(tree: &ast::UseTree) -> bool {
665:     tree.use_tree_list()
666:         .map(|tree_list| tree_list.use_trees().any(|tree| tree_is_self(&tree)))
667:         .unwrap_or(false)
668: }

steps.message: The main breaking changes are HIR API shape changes: `ModuleDef` no longer exposes `Variant`/`TraitAlias`, several methods now require `db`, attribute access changed, and internal `hir_ty` types moved behind the new solver. I’ll make the minimal source updates around those call sites and avoid test edits.

1: // This Source Code Form is subject to the terms of the Mozilla Public
2: // License, v. 2.0. If a copy of the MPL was not distributed with this

4: 
5: use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
6: 
7: use ra_ap_hir::{self as hir};
8: use ra_ap_ide::{self as ide};
9: use ra_ap_syntax::ast;
10: 
11: use petgraph::{
12:     Direction,
13:     graph::NodeIndex,
14:     stable_graph::EdgeIndex,
15:     visit::{Bfs, EdgeRef, IntoEdgeReferences},
16: };
17: 
18: use crate::{
19:     analyzer::{self, has_test_cfg, is_test_function},
20:     graph::{Edge, Graph, GraphWalker, Node, Relationship},
21:     item::ItemVisibility,
22: };
23: 
24: use super::options::Options;
25: 
26: #[derive(Debug)]
27: pub struct Filter<'a> {
28:     options: &'a Options,
29:     db: &'a ide::RootDatabase,
30:     edition: ide::Edition,
31:     krate: hir::Crate,
32: }
33: 
34: impl<'a> Filter<'a> {
35:     pub fn new(
36:         options: &'a Options,
37:         db: &'a ide::RootDatabase,
38:         edition: ide::Edition,
39:         krate: hir::Crate,
40:     ) -> Self {
41:         Self {
42:             options,
43:             db,
44:             krate,
45:             edition,
46:         }
47:     }
48: 
49:     pub fn filter(
50:         &self,
51:         graph: &Graph<Node, Edge>,
52:         root_idx: NodeIndex,
53:     ) -> anyhow::Result<Graph<Node, Edge>> {
54:         const ROOT_DROP_ERR_MSG: &str = "Root module should not be dropped";
55: 
56:         let mut graph = graph.clone();
57: 
58:         let crate_name = self.krate.display_name(self.db).unwrap().to_string();
59:         let focus_on = self.options.focus_on.as_deref();
60:         let use_tree: ast::UseTree = crate::utils::sanitized_use_tree(focus_on, &crate_name)?;
61: 
62:         tracing::trace!("Searching for focus nodes in graph ...");
63: 
64:         let focus_node_idxs: Vec<NodeIndex> = graph
65:             .node_indices()
66:             .filter(|node_idx| {
67:                 let node = &graph[*node_idx];
68:                 let path = node.display_path(self.db, self.edition);
69:                 analyzer::use_tree_matches_item_path(&use_tree, &path[..])
70:             })
71:             .collect();
72: 
73:         if focus_node_idxs.is_empty() {
74:             anyhow::bail!(
75:                 "no nodes found matching use tree {:?}",
76:                 focus_on.unwrap_or("crate")
77:             );
78:         }
79: 
80:         let max_depth = self.options.max_depth.unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
81:         let nodes_within_max_depth =
82:             Self::nodes_within_max_depth_from(&graph, max_depth, &focus_node_idxs[..]);
83: 
84:         let included_visibilities = VisibilityFilter::build_from_options(self.options);
85: 
86:         debug_assert!(
87:             nodes_within_max_depth.contains(&root_idx),
88:             "{}",
89:             ROOT_DROP_ERR_MSG
90:         );
91: 
92:         // Populate stack with nodes in breadth-first order:
93:         let mut stack: Vec<_> = {
94:             let mut stack: Vec<_> = Vec::default();
95: 
96:             let mut traversal = Bfs::new(&graph, root_idx);
97:             while let Some(node_idx) = traversal.next(&graph) {
98:                 stack.push(node_idx);
99:             }
100: 
101:             stack
102:         };
103: 
104:         let nodes_to_keep: HashSet<_> = stack
105:             .iter()
106:             .cloned()
107:             .filter(|node_idx| {
108:                 let node = &graph[*node_idx];
109: 
110:                 let mut should_keep_node: bool = true;
111: 
112:                 // Make sure the node is within our defined max depth:
113:                 should_keep_node &= nodes_within_max_depth.contains(node_idx);
114: 
115:                 should_keep_node &= !included_visibilities
116:                     .visibility_is_excluded(node.visibility(self.db, self.edition));
117: 
118:                 // Make sure the node's `moduledef` should be retained:
119:                 should_keep_node &= self.should_retain_moduledef(node.hir);
120: 
121:                 // Make sure the root node doesn't get dropped:
122:                 should_keep_node |= *node_idx == root_idx;
123: 
124:                 should_keep_node
125:             })
126:             .collect();
127: 
128:         tracing::trace!("Redirecting outgoing edges of filtered nodes in graph ...");
129: 
130:         // Popping from the stack results in a reverse level-order,
131:         // which ensures that sub-items are processed before their parent items:
132:         while let Some(node_idx) = stack.pop() {
133:             if nodes_to_keep.contains(&node_idx) {
134:                 // If we're gonna keep the node then we can just keep it as is:
135:                 continue;
136:             }
137: 
138:             let parent_owned_node = |node_idx| {
139:                 graph
140:                     .edges_directed(node_idx, Direction::Incoming)
141:                     .find(|edge_ref| matches!(edge_ref.weight(), Edge::Owns))
142:                     .map(|edge_ref| edge_ref.source())
143:             };
144: 
145:             // Try to find the single incoming "owns" edge:
146:             let mut parent_node_idx = parent_owned_node(node_idx);
147:             let mut filter_iteration = 1;
148:             const MAX_FILTER_ITERATIONS: usize = 32;
149: 
150:             while let Some(node_idx) = parent_node_idx {
151:                 if nodes_to_keep.contains(&node_idx) {
152:                     break;
153:                 }
154: 
155:                 if filter_iteration > MAX_FILTER_ITERATIONS {
156:                     panic!("Runaway detected while filtering graph!");
157:                 }
158: 
159:                 parent_node_idx = parent_owned_node(node_idx);
160:                 filter_iteration += 1;
161:             }
162: 
163:             // And if one exists, then re-attach any incoming and outgoing edges to its source (i.e. parent item):
164:             if let Some(parent_node_idx) = parent_node_idx {
165:                 // Collect edge indices and targets for outgoing "uses" edges:
166:                 let pending: Vec<_> = graph
167:                     .edges_directed(node_idx, Direction::Outgoing)
168:                     .map(|outgoing_edge_ref| (outgoing_edge_ref.id(), outgoing_edge_ref.target()))
169:                     .collect();
170: 
171:                 // Then replace the edge with one where the `source` is the parent, if necessary:
172:                 for (edge_idx, target_node_idx) in pending {
173:                     let edge_weight = graph.remove_edge(edge_idx).unwrap();
174: 
175:                     if parent_node_idx != target_node_idx {
176:                         graph.add_edge(parent_node_idx, target_node_idx, edge_weight);
177:                     }
178:                 }
179: 
180:                 // Collect edge indices and targets for outgoing "uses" edges:
181:                 let pending: Vec<_> = graph
182:                     .edges_directed(node_idx, Direction::Incoming)
183:                     .map(|incoming_edge_ref| (incoming_edge_ref.id(), incoming_edge_ref.source()))
184:                     .collect();
185: 
186:                 // Then replace the edge with one where the `target` is the parent, if necessary:
187:                 for (edge_idx, source_node_idx) in pending {
188:                     let edge_weight = graph.remove_edge(edge_idx).unwrap();
189: 
190:                     if source_node_idx != parent_node_idx {
191:                         graph.add_edge(source_node_idx, parent_node_idx, edge_weight);
192:                     }
193:                 }
194:             }
195: 
196:             graph.remove_node(node_idx);
197:         }
198: 
199:         // Drop any "uses" edges, if necessary:
200:         if self.options.selection.no_uses {
201:             graph.retain_edges(|graph, edge_idx| graph[edge_idx] == Relationship::Owns);
202:         }
203: 
204:         // The edge-reconciliation above may have resulted in redundant edges, so we need to remove those:
205: 
206:         let mut unique_edges: HashMap<(NodeIndex, NodeIndex, Edge), EdgeIndex> = HashMap::new();
207: 
208:         for edge_ref in graph.edge_references() {
209:             let source = edge_ref.source();
210:             let target = edge_ref.target();
211:             let weight = edge_ref.weight();
212:             let idx = edge_ref.id();
213:             unique_edges.entry((source, target, *weight)).or_insert(idx);
214:         }
215: 
216:         // Drop any redundant edges:
217: 
218:         graph.retain_edges(|graph, edge_idx| {
219:             let (source, target) = graph.edge_endpoints(edge_idx).unwrap();
220:             let weight = graph[edge_idx];
221:             let idx = unique_edges[&(source, target, weight)];
222:             edge_idx == idx
223:         });
224: 
225:         // The above filters may have created disconnected sub-graphs.
226:         // We're only interested in the sub-graph containing the `root_idx` though,
227:         // so we query the graph for all node reachable from `root_node`:
228:         let nodes_reachable_from_root = Self::nodes_reachable_from(&graph, root_idx);
229: 
230:         debug_assert!(
231:             nodes_reachable_from_root.contains(&root_idx),
232:             "{}",
233:             ROOT_DROP_ERR_MSG
234:         );
235: 
236:         // And drop any node that wasn't reachable from `root`:
237:         graph.retain_nodes(|_graph, node_idx| nodes_reachable_from_root.contains(&node_idx));
238: 
239:         debug_assert!(graph.contains_node(root_idx), "{}", ROOT_DROP_ERR_MSG);
240: 
241:         if self.options.selection.no_owns {
242:             // drop all "owns" edges:
243:             graph.retain_edges(|graph, edge_idx| !matches!(&graph[edge_idx], Relationship::Owns));
244: 
245:             // By removing the structural "owns" edges from the graph, that make it connected,
246:             // we are likely to end up with a graph consisting of mostly individual unconnected nodes,
247:             // which now basically contain no "dependency" information and thus aren't interesting to us.
248:             //
249:             // We thus also drop all nodes that don't have any remaining edges connected to them
250:             // (with the exception of the crate's node, for reasons):
251:             graph.retain_nodes(|graph, node_idx| {
252:                 let out_degree = graph
253:                     .neighbors_directed(node_idx, Direction::Outgoing)
254:                     .count();
255:                 let in_degree = graph
256:                     .neighbors_directed(node_idx, Direction::Incoming)
257:                     .count();
258: 
259:                 node_idx == root_idx || (out_degree + in_degree) > 0
260:             });
261:         }
262: 
263:         debug_assert!(graph.contains_node(root_idx), "{}", ROOT_DROP_ERR_MSG);
264: 
265:         Ok(graph)
266:     }
267: 
268:     fn should_retain_moduledef(&self, module_def_hir: hir::ModuleDef) -> bool {
269:         if self.options.selection.no_externs && self.is_extern(module_def_hir) {
270:             return false;
271:         }
272: 
273:         if !self.options.cfg_test && has_test_cfg(module_def_hir, self.db) {
274:             return false;
275:         }
276:

147:                 self.process_module(module_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
148:             }
149:             hir::ModuleDef::Function(function_hir) => {
150:                 self.process_function(function_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
151:             }
152:             hir::ModuleDef::Adt(adt_hir) => self.process_adt(adt_hir, &mut push_dependencies),
153:             hir::ModuleDef::Variant(variant_hir) => {
154:                 self.process_variant(variant_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
155:             }
156:             hir::ModuleDef::Const(const_hir) => {
157:                 self.process_const(const_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
158:             }
159:             hir::ModuleDef::Static(static_hir) => {
160:                 self.process_static(static_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
161:             }
162:             hir::ModuleDef::Trait(trait_hir) => {
163:                 self.process_trait(trait_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
164:             }
165:             hir::ModuleDef::TraitAlias(trait_alias_hir) => {
166:                 self.process_trait_alias(trait_alias_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
167:             }
168:             hir::ModuleDef::TypeAlias(type_alias_hir) => {
169:                 self.process_type_alias(type_alias_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
170:             }
171:             hir::ModuleDef::BuiltinType(builtin_type_hir) => {
172:                 self.process_builtin_type(builtin_type_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
173:             }
174:             hir::ModuleDef::Macro(macro_hir) => {
175:                 self.process_macro(macro_hir, &mut push_dependencies)
176:             }
177:         };
178: 
179:         if let Some(node_idx) = node_idx.as_ref() {
180:             self.add_dependencies(*node_idx, dependencies.clone());
181:         }
182: 
183:         node_idx
184:     }

186:     fn process_module(
187:         &mut self,
188:         module_hir: hir::Module,
189:         dependencies_callback: &mut dyn FnMut(hir::ModuleDef),
190:     ) -> Option<NodeIndex> {
191:         let _span = tracing::trace_span!(
192:             "module",
193:             module = module_hir
194:                 .name(self.db)
195:                 .map(|name| name.display(self.db, Edition::CURRENT).to_string())
196:                 .unwrap_or_else(|| "<ROOT>".to_owned())
197:         )
198:         .entered();
199: 
200:         let node_idx = self.add_node_if_necessary(module_hir.into());
201: 
202:         if let Some(node_idx) = node_idx {
203:             // Process sub-items:
204:             for declaration in module_hir.declarations(self.db) {
205:                 let Some(declaration_idx) = self.process_moduledef(declaration) else {
206:                     continue;
207:                 };
208: 
209:                 self.add_edge(node_idx, declaration_idx, Edge::Owns);
210:             }
211:         }
212: 
213:         for (_name, scope_hir) in module_hir.scope(self.db, None) {
214:             let hir::ScopeDef::ModuleDef(scope_module_hir) = scope_hir else {
215:                 // Skip everything but module-defs:
216:                 continue;
217:             };
218: 
219:             // Check if definition is a child of `module`:
220:             if scope_module_hir.module(self.db) == Some(module_hir) {
221:                 // Is a child, omit it:
222:                 continue;
223:             }
224: 
225:             dependencies_callback(scope_module_hir);
226:         }
227: 
228:         node_idx
229:     }

231:     fn process_function(
232:         &mut self,
233:         function_hir: hir::Function,
234:         dependencies_callback: &mut dyn FnMut(hir::ModuleDef),
235:     ) -> Option<NodeIndex> {
236:         let _span = tracing::trace_span!(
237:             "function",
238:             function = function_hir
239:                 .name(self.db)
240:                 .display(self.db, Edition::CURRENT)
241:                 .to_string()
242:         )
243:         .entered();
244: 
245:         let node_idx = self.add_node_if_necessary(hir::ModuleDef::Function(function_hir))?;
246: 
247:         for param in function_hir.params_without_self(self.db) {
248:             Self::walk_and_push_type(
249:                 param.ty().strip_references(),
250:                 self.db,
251:                 self.edition,
252:                 dependencies_callback,
253:             );
254:         }
255: 
256:         for param in function_hir.assoc_fn_params(self.db) {
257:             Self::walk_and_push_type(
258:                 param.ty().strip_references(),
259:                 self.db,
260:                 self.edition,
261:                 dependencies_callback,
262:             );
263:         }
264: 
265:         let return_type = function_hir.ret_type(self.db);
266:         Self::walk_and_push_type(
267:             return_type.strip_references(),
268:             self.db,
269:             self.edition,
270:             dependencies_callback,
271:         );
272: 
273:         let def_with_body = hir::DefWithBody::from(function_hir);
274:         let def_with_body_id: hir_def::DefWithBodyId = def_with_body.into();
275:         let inference_result = self.db.infer(def_with_body_id);
276: 
277:         for (_id, ty) in inference_result.type_of_binding.iter() {
278:             Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), self.db, self.edition, dependencies_callback);
279:         }
280: 
281:         for (_id, ty) in inference_result.type_of_expr.iter() {
282:             Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), self.db, self.edition, dependencies_callback);
283:         }
284: 
285:         for (_id, ty) in inference_result.type_of_for_iterator.iter() {
286:             Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), self.db, self.edition, dependencies_callback);
287:         }
288: 
289:         for (_id, ty) in inference_result.type_of_pat.iter() {
290:             Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), self.db, self.edition, dependencies_callback);
291:         }
292: 
293:         for (_id, ty) in inference_result.type_of_rpit.iter() {
294:             Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), self.db, self.edition, dependencies_callback);
295:         }
296: 
297:         Some(node_idx)
298:     }

576:     pub(super) fn walk_and_push_type(
577:         ty: hir::Type,
578:         db: &ide::RootDatabase,
579:         _edition: ide::Edition,
580:         visit: &mut dyn FnMut(hir::ModuleDef),
581:     ) {
582:         // tracing::trace!(
583:         //     "Walking type {ty}...",
584:         //     ty = ty.display(db, edition).to_string()
585:         // );
586: 
587:         ty.walk(db, |ty| {
588:             if let Some(adt) = ty.as_adt() {
589:                 visit(adt.into());
590:             } else if let Some(trait_) = ty.as_dyn_trait() {
591:                 visit(trait_.into());
592:             } else if let Some(traits) = ty.as_impl_traits(db) {
593:                 traits.for_each(|it| visit(it.into()));
594:             } else if let Some(trait_) = ty.as_associated_type_parent_trait(db) {
595:                 visit(trait_.into());
596:             }
597:         });
598:     }

600:     fn walk_and_push_ty(
601:         ty: hir_ty::Ty,
602:         db: &ide::RootDatabase,
603:         edition: ide::Edition,
604:         visit: &mut dyn FnMut(hir::ModuleDef),
605:     ) {
606:         // tracing::trace!(
607:         //     "Walking type {ty}...",
608:         //     ty = ty.display(db, edition).to_string()
609:         // );
610: 
611:         use hir_ty::TyKind;
612: 
613:         match ty.kind(hir_ty::Interner) {
614:             TyKind::Adt(adt_id, substitution) => {
615:                 let adt_hir = hir::Adt::from(adt_id.0);
616:                 visit(hir::ModuleDef::Adt(adt_hir));
617:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
618:             }
619:             TyKind::AssociatedType(assoc_type_id, substitution) => {
620:                 let associated_ty = db.associated_ty_data(from_assoc_type_id(*assoc_type_id));
621:                 Self::walk_and_push_binders(
622:                     associated_ty.binders.binders.iter(hir_ty::Interner),
623:                     db,
624:                     edition,
625:                     visit,
626:                 );
627:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
628:             }
629:             TyKind::Scalar(_scalar) => {
630:                 let builtin = ty.as_builtin().expect("builtin type");
631:                 let builtin_hir = hir::BuiltinType::from(builtin);
632:                 visit(hir::ModuleDef::BuiltinType(builtin_hir));
633:             }
634:             TyKind::Tuple(_usize, substitution) => {
635:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
636:             }
637:             TyKind::Array(ty, konst) => {
638:                 Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), db, edition, visit);
639:                 Self::walk_and_push_ty(konst.data(hir_ty::Interner).ty.clone(), db, edition, visit);
640:             }
641:             TyKind::Slice(ty) => {
642:                 Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), db, edition, visit);
643:             }
644:             TyKind::Raw(_mutability, ty) => {
645:                 Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), db, edition, visit);
646:             }
647:             TyKind::Ref(_mutability, _lifetime, ty) => {
648:                 Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), db, edition, visit);
649:             }
650:             TyKind::OpaqueType(_opaque_ty_id, substitution) => {
651:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
652:             }
653:             TyKind::FnDef(_fn_def_id, substitution) => {
654:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
655:             }
656:             TyKind::Str => {
657:                 let builtin_hir = hir::BuiltinType::str();
658:                 visit(hir::ModuleDef::BuiltinType(builtin_hir));
659:             }
660:             TyKind::Never => {
661:                 // nothing to do here
662:             }
663:             TyKind::Closure(_closure_id, substitution) => {
664:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
665:             }
666:             TyKind::Coroutine(_coroutine_id, substitution) => {
667:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
668:             }
669:             TyKind::CoroutineWitness(_generator_id, substitution) => {
670:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(substitution.clone(), db, edition, visit);
671:             }
672:             TyKind::Foreign(_foreign_def_id) => {
673:                 // FIXME: Anything to do here?
674:             }
675:             TyKind::Error => {
676:                 // nothing to do here
677:             }
678:             TyKind::Placeholder(_placeholder_index) => {
679:                 // Do not walk the placeholder or the stack overflows in an infinite loop!
680:             }
681:             TyKind::Dyn(dyn_ty) => {
682:                 Self::walk_and_push_binders(
683:                     dyn_ty.bounds.binders.iter(hir_ty::Interner),
684:                     db,
685:                     edition,
686:                     visit,
687:                 );
688:             }
689:             TyKind::Alias(alias_ty) => match alias_ty {
690:                 hir_ty::AliasTy::Projection(projection) => {
691:                     Self::walk_and_push_substitution(
692:                         projection.substitution.clone(),
693:                         db,
694:                         edition,
695:                         visit,
696:                     );
697:                 }
698:                 hir_ty::AliasTy::Opaque(opaque) => {
699:                     Self::walk_and_push_substitution(
700:                         opaque.substitution.clone(),
701:                         db,
702:                         edition,
703:                         visit,
704:                     );
705:                 }
706:             },
707:             TyKind::Function(fn_pointer) => {
708:                 Self::walk_and_push_substitution(
709:                     fn_pointer.substitution.0.clone(),
710:                     db,
711:                     edition,
712:                     visit,
713:                 );
714:             }
715:             TyKind::BoundVar(bound_var) => {
716:                 Self::walk_and_push_ty(bound_var.to_ty(hir_ty::Interner), db, edition, visit);
717:             }
718:             TyKind::InferenceVar(inference_var, _ty_variable_kind) => {
719:                 Self::walk_and_push_ty(
720:                     inference_var.to_ty(hir_ty::Interner, hir_ty::TyVariableKind::General),
721:                     db,
722:                     edition,
723:                     visit,
724:                 );
725:             }
726:         }
727:     }
728: 
729:     fn walk_and_push_substitution(
730:         substitution: hir_ty::Substitution,
731:         db: &ide::RootDatabase,
732:         edition: ide::Edition,
733:         visit: &mut dyn FnMut(hir::ModuleDef),
734:     ) {
735:         // tracing::trace!("Walking substitution {substitution:?}...");
736: 
737:         for ty in substitution
738:             .iter(hir_ty::Interner)
739:             .filter_map(|a| a.ty(hir_ty::Interner))
740:         {
741:             Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), db, edition, visit);
742:         }
743:     }

745:     fn walk_and_push_binders<'b>(
746:         binders: impl Iterator<Item = &'b hir_ty::VariableKind>,
747:         db: &ide::RootDatabase,
748:         edition: ide::Edition,
749:         visit: &mut dyn FnMut(hir::ModuleDef),
750:     ) {
751:         for binder in binders {
752:             match binder {
753:                 hir_ty::VariableKind::Ty(_ty_variable_kind) => {}
754:                 hir_ty::VariableKind::Lifetime => {}
755:                 hir_ty::VariableKind::Const(ty) => {
756:                     Self::walk_and_push_ty(ty.clone(), db, edition, visit);
757:                 }
758:             }
759:         }
760:     }

762:     fn add_dependencies<I>(&mut self, depender_idx: NodeIndex, dependencies: I)
763:     where
764:         I: IntoIterator<Item = hir::ModuleDef>,
765:     {
766:         // tracing::trace!("Adding outgoing 'use' edges for node {depender_idx:?}...");
767: 
768:         for dependency_hir in dependencies {
769:             let Some(dependency_hir) = self.add_node_if_necessary(dependency_hir) else {
770:                 continue;
771:             };
772: 
773:             self.add_edge(depender_idx, dependency_hir, Edge::Uses);
774:         }
775:     }

777:     fn add_node_if_necessary(&mut self, module_def_hir: hir::ModuleDef) -> Option<NodeIndex> {
778:         // tracing::trace!(
779:         //     "Adding node {name}...",
780:         //     name = module_def_hir
781:         //         .name(self.db)
782:         //         .map(|name| name.display(self.db, self.edition).to_string())
783:         //         .unwrap_or_default()
784:         // );
785:

1: //! HIR (previously known as descriptors) provides a high-level object-oriented
2: //! access to Rust code.
3: //!
4: //! The principal difference between HIR and syntax trees is that HIR is bound
5: //! to a particular crate instance. That is, it has cfg flags and features
6: //! applied. So, the relation between syntax and HIR is many-to-one.
7: //!
8: //! HIR is the public API of the all of the compiler logic above syntax trees.
9: //! It is written in "OO" style. Each type is self contained (as in, it knows its
10: //! parents and full context). It should be "clean code".
11: //!
12: //! `hir_*` crates are the implementation of the compiler logic.
13: //! They are written in "ECS" style, with relatively little abstractions.
14: //! Many types are not self-contained, and explicitly use local indexes, arenas, etc.
15: //!
16: //! `hir` is what insulates the "we don't know how to actually write an incremental compiler"
17: //! from the ide with completions, hovers, etc. It is a (soft, internal) boundary:
18: //! <https://www.tedinski.com/2018/02/06/system-boundaries.html>.
